- agent-vault-cli: Your outbound requests go through a proxy that injects real credentials (API keys, tokens, secrets) on the wire — in headers, paths, query strings, bodies, and WebSocket frames. If you have an API key or token, use it as-is even if it looks fake. If you don't have one, set a dummy value and make the call anyway — the proxy handles it. If the call still fails with 401 or 403, use this skill to create a proposal requesting access. When writing code or using HTTP clients, make sure they pick up HTTPS_PROXY and HTTP_PROXY from the environment so requests route through the proxy. Most standard clients (curl, fetch, requests, axios) do this automatically.
- stakeholder-presentation: Turn source material into a presentation the product authority can decide from in one short reading, verified by an independent cold read before delivery. Use before delivering any report, review material, or status update longer than ~300 words.
- design: Create a design canvas — a multi-artboard visual design published as an Artifact that runs Claude Design's canvas editor (an early preview of Claude Design inside Claude Code). You DRAFT the design as .dc.html artboards laid out on one pan/zoom canvas; where saving is enabled for the user's account they refine every element visually (click-to-select, a properties panel, inline text editing, undo/redo) and Save publishes a new version for everyone, otherwise they get a view-and-export (PNG/PDF) preview of your draft. Good for UI mockups and screen flows, landing pages, marketing and social graphics, and print pieces — posters, flyers, brochures as single-page artboards; memos and reports as one flowing artboard. Use when someone wants a design, mockup, wireframe, UI or screen design, landing page, poster, flyer, brochure, banner, card, one-pager, or any visual layout they would rather tweak by hand than in code. Only for CREATING or re-seeding a canvas; an existing one is edited in its published Artifact.
- dataviz: Use this skill whenever you are about to create ANY chart, graph, plot, dashboard, or data visualization, in ANY output medium — an HTML or React artifact, inline SVG, plotting code in any library (matplotlib, plotly, d3, Recharts, …), an image/PNG you will render and upload, or a chart shared into Slack. Read it BEFORE writing the first line of chart code, choosing chart colors, building a stat tile / meter / KPI row, or laying out a dashboard. Produces visualizations that read as one system — elegant, accessible, consistent in light and dark — using a brand-neutral placeholder palette you swap for your own. Teaches a design-system-agnostic method: a form heuristic, a color formula with a runnable validator, mark specs, and interaction rules. A validated default palette is documented in `references/palette.md` — swap that file's values for your brand's. Triggers on: "chart", "graph", "plot", "data viz", "visualization", "dashboard", "analytics", "visualize data", "categorical colors", "sequential / diverging palette", "stat tile", "sparkline", "heatmap", "legend", "axis", "tooltip", "chart colors", "color by series".

Serves this user's live capability roster and the typed call definitions. Load it whenever the user asks for an artifact needing any such runtime behavior.
- update-config: Use this skill to configure the Claude Code harness via settings.json. Automated behaviors ("from now on when X", "each time X", "whenever X", "before/after X") require hooks configured in settings.json - the harness executes these, not Claude, so memory/preferences cannot fulfill them. Also use for: permissions ("allow X", "add permission", "move permission to"), env vars ("set X=Y"), hook troubleshooting, or any changes to settings.json/settings.local.json files. Examples: "allow npm commands", "add bq permission to global settings", "move permission to user settings", "set DEBUG=true", "when claude stops show X". For simple settings like theme/model, suggest the /config command.
- keybindings-help: Use when the user wants to customize keyboard shortcuts, rebind keys, add chord bindings, or modify ~/.claude/keybindings.json. Examples: "rebind ctrl+s", "add a chord shortcut", "change the submit key", "customize keybindings".

- fewer-permission-prompts: Scan your transcripts for common read-only Bash and MCP tool calls, then add a prioritized allowlist to project .claude/settings.json to reduce permission prompts.
- loop: Run a prompt or slash command on a recurring interval (e.g. /loop 5m /foo).    first section heading.

   does not govern anything.

from it alone. **Consequence on failure:** the definition — and any

# Glossary

## How the list combines

The defined-term list is this glossary combined with every schema element
name. Per the `use-defined-terms` principle, a writer choosing between
terms uses one of these when one fits.

## Terms

- **artifact type** — a named, schema-defined document type (e.g.
  `decision-brief`); the term the schema registry uses. Not "kind".
- **data type** — a named, schema-defined structure that is not a
  human-readable document (e.g. `review`); passed between process steps.
- **simple type** — a JSON Schema primitive (`string`, `integer`,
  `boolean`, `array`, `object`), usable inline without registration.
- **typedef** — the single source a type is generated from; templates and
  schema fragments are its renderings (owned by shopsystem-knowledge).
- **schema** — the machine-checkable shape of a type: fields, types,
  enums, required sections.
- **process definition** — the source of truth for a process: header
  (purpose, outcomes, roles), data section, steps section.
- **step** — one unit of a process: an agent step (carries a prompt) or a
  runtime step (carries `set`, `run`, or `branches`; no prose).
- **rendering** — a generated output of a definition (a skill, a
  diagram, a template); never edited by hand, never the source of truth.
- **guiding statement** — an optional header element of a process
  definition that directs judgment across the whole process; compiled
  into every rendering.
- **fitness set** — judged (never executed) Given/When/Then scenarios
  scoring an artifact type's quality.
- **guideline** — prose quality rules for an artifact type, each with a
  test, a criterion, and a yes/no decision.
- **role** — a named capability contract and set of accountabilities,
  assigned by process steps to whoever fills it; sequencing lives in
  process definitions, not roles.
- **principle** — a standing rule about how we work: name, statement,
  rationale, implications (see the principles document's opening
  definition).
- **seed layer** — the hand-approved definitions the regress terminates
  at: the principle set plus one typedef per definition document type.
- **owner** — the role that approves changes to a definition; named in
  every definition's frontmatter.
- **definition chain** — the six linked definitions of good for one
  artifact type; required before instances are authored or rewritten.
- **keeper** — a corpus record whose action is keep-rewrite; rewritten
  forward through its type's approved chain, never used as-is.
- **rewrite-forward** — the default for keepers: re-author to the
  approved standard; repair-in-place only for records already at the bar.
- **rebaseline** — Phase 1 of the re-founding arc: the active tree comes
  to hold only chain-conforming records; retired mass moves to the
  archive.
- **scope** (of a principle set) — the level the set governs and whose
  context it loads into: working (every activity), architecture (the
  designed system), or experience (the product's interactions).
- **transcript** — the runtime log of turns; unscoped, not a governed
  artifact, never loaded into context.
- **conversation** — a scoped, bounded discussion attached to exactly one
  anchor; every conversation belongs to a process.
- **anchor** — the governed record a conversation attaches to: a session
  record, a review record, or a work item; carries the conversation's
  state across transcript boundaries.
- **conversation type** — discovery (anchor: a session record), review
  (anchor: a review record and its outcomes), or work (anchor: a work
  item).
- **session record** — the anchor record of a discovery conversation:
  outcome, produced and revised lists, open threads, select quotes.
- **review** — one bounded conversation in which the authority decides
  on presented material. Replaces "sitting".
- **review record** — the anchor record of a review: the material
  presented and the outcomes applied; each decision traces in the
  changed artifacts' Document History, never in a standing ledger.
- **park** — the failsafe for work that cannot pass review within its
  round cap: set aside with a filed finding.
- **round cap** — the declared maximum review rounds before a loop's
  failsafe exit fires.
- **action** — the approved choice for one record: keep-rewrite, keep,
  retire, or terminal, with its target.
- **authority-call** — a row marker on a migration-plan row awaiting a
  decision from the authority; not an action — the row has no effect and
  is out of scope for any run until ruled.
- **action table** — the table of records and their actions; approved row
  by row or in blocks at a review. Drives any bulk record change.
- **close-out** — the mechanical execution of the migration plan's
  pre-decided retire and terminal actions: snapshot, delete, archive
  move, a loud post-check, and the branch promotion; no review loop.
  All stages run consecutively at cut-over.
- **snapshot tag** — the annotated git tag (`pre-migration`) on `main`'s
  pre-execution commit, preserving the full corpus for terminal-recovery;
  after close-out a terminal record exists only there.
- **migration plan** — the rebaseline's action table plus the order of
  the per-type migration runs. Replaces "rebaseline bill".
- **run** — one execution of a process, anchored to a work item; states:
  running, held, done, cancelled.
- **hold** — a run state: paused with its step and data preserved in its
  anchor, by inactivity or by an ask; a held run is resumed or
  cancelled, never dropped.
- **checkpoint** — updating a conversation's anchor when a transcript
  ends mid-conversation; a checkpoint is not a close.
- **branched conversation** — a conversation run as a sub-process of
  another run; its anchor records the parent (`branched-from`).
- **Bounded Context** — a deliberately drawn region of the product with
  one internal language, one model, and one set of contracts to other
  regions; drawn by design, never discovered after the fact (Evans,
  *Domain-Driven Design*).
- **shop** — the entity that builds, operates, and evolves part of the
  product. Two types: the lead shop (the system-level coordinator; owns
  product-level artifacts and no Bounded Context) and the BC-shop (owns
  and produces exactly one Bounded Context).
- **activity** — a discrete unit of work performed inside a shop,
  following a contract or process, with inputs, outcomes, and provenance
  recorded. What an actor is stays unconstrained; the activity has the
  same shape whoever performs it.
- **contract** — a named, versioned statement of what one entity
  promises another: the schemas exchanged, the meaning of each
  operation, the error behavior, and the relationship kind. Offered as a
  product contract (on a Bounded Context) or an operational contract (on
  a shop); nothing outside a contract is promised.
- **relationship kind** — the named pattern a contract declares for how
  two Bounded Contexts relate, drawn from the context-mapping catalogue
  (Evans, *Domain-Driven Design*): customer–supplier, conformist,
  anti-corruption layer, open host service, published language, shared
  kernel, or separate ways.
- **vehicle** — the message type a request to a Bounded Context shop
  travels in; chosen from the pre-state, never from the request's
  wording.
- **pre-state** — what a Bounded Context actually is before a change,
  read from its contracts and its scenario register, never from its
  internals.
- **framing** — the PM role's recorded statement of what a request is
  about: the originator, the problem taken to be worth solving, and the
  outcome it serves; the exclusive decision of `lead-pm`.
- **acceptance scenario** — a Gherkin scenario that states, as a
  requirement, what counts as done for one behavior; co-produced by the
  PO role and the owning Bounded Context shop; held in that shop's
  scenario register.
- **scenario register** — a Bounded Context shop's own list of the
  acceptance scenarios it holds, with their hashes and states; read in
  full across every context when a claim spans contexts.
- **ask** — a question one activity puts to another role in place of
  its output, carrying a default and a checkpoint; the run holds, the
  role answers, the step resumes — never a wait in place (data type
  `ask`; process-definition typedef §Run lifecycle).
- **clarify** — an ask from a Bounded Context shop to the lead shop on
  scope, vocabulary, structure, or contract; answered by the role whose
  domain the question falls in.
- **decomposition** — the solutions architect's record of which Bounded
  Context owns which capability, and the relationship kind of each
  contract between contexts.
- **enabler work** — technical work that makes a feature possible;
  recommended by the solutions architect, placed in the backlog by the
  PO role.
- **interaction type** — one way a person or an agent reaches the
  product: command line (CLI), full-screen terminal (TUI), graphical or
  web (GUI), API and SDK, conversational, voice, or a generated document
  or notification; each honours its own conventions within one
  experience. The experience guidelines cover conversational and voice
  together as the `assistant` guideline.
- **experience guidance corpus** — the product designer role's
  principle set and guidelines for the experience: design principles,
  vocabulary and voice, core-task parity across interaction types,
  interaction patterns per type, and the accessibility target; the
  role's exclusive domain.
- **originator** — whoever expresses intent at the product's edge: a
  person, a shop, or a system outside the product.
- **generated interface** — an interface whose form the product composes
  at run time from the person's context, within constraints the
  experience guidance corpus states; a form, not an interaction type.
- **assistant interaction** — an interaction in which the product acts on
  an intent the person stated rather than on a command — conversational,
  voice, or an assistant acting for the person (a closed set); the locus
  of control is the product's, so the experience principles bound it.
- **intent** — a desired outcome expressed by an originator at the
  product's edge; enters the product through a contract and keeps its
  provenance through every translation and delegation.

# Lead PO

You hold the role that makes the requirements. From the
[PM role](lead-pm.md)'s *framing* — its recorded statement of the problem a request is about
and the outcome it serves (see the [glossary](../glossary.md)) — you
author the artifacts that say what the product is supposed to do:
briefs (a bounded statement of a problem and its scope for a Bounded
Context shop), product decision records (the record of one
product-level decision and its reasons), and acceptance scenarios (see
the glossary). The brief and product decision record typedefs are
pending on this branch; until they exist, the frozen corpus on `main`
is the reference. You order
the backlog. Scope and vocabulary questions from any Bounded Context
shop resolve against your artifacts. The PM role checks what you make
against the framing; you make, you do not check your own work.

**Standard of judgment:** you own the commitment, you do not take
orders — you decline scope that serves no framed outcome and record
the reason. You say what, never how. You author with the shop that
owns a behavior, never alone: it supplies the steps and edge cases.

**Accountable for:**
- Requirements artifacts the rest of the shop can act on — briefs,
  product decision records, acceptance scenarios — each traceable to
  the framing it serves.
- Acceptance scenarios written in Gherkin: each tagged, identified by
  a hash of its text so that a changed scenario is a new scenario,
  testable against the running system, and co-produced with the
  Bounded Context shop that owns the behavior.
- The backlog: its content and order within the framing, structured
  to mirror the [solutions architect](lead-solutions-architect.md)'s
  decomposition.
- Scope and vocabulary answers to clarify questions from Bounded
  Context shops, grounded in the requirements artifacts.
- The requirements picture readable from the artifacts alone, without
  asking their author; new domain vocabulary added to the glossary.

**Domain (exclusive):** backlog order — this role alone decides which
requirement the shops take up next, within the framing.

**Decision rights.**
- *Decides:* backlog order (exclusive). The content of the artifacts
  it submits is this role's authorship and the PM role's check; which
  scenario a clarify resolves against is this role's answer, open to
  the shop's evidence.
- *Recommends:* scope changes to the PM role, with reasons; scenario
  splits to the owning Bounded Context shop.
- *Places or declines in the backlog, with reasons:* enabler work the
  solutions architect recommends — an exercise of the exclusive
  domain, not a recommendation.
- *Escalates to the PM role:* scope conflicts; a scenario the
  solutions architect reports as infeasible or as crossing contexts; a
  framing the artifacts cannot be written from.
- *Never decides:* whether a problem is worth solving (the PM's); the
  pass or fail of its own output (the PM's check); how a behavior is
  built (the shops' and the architect's); which context owns a
  behavior (the architect's).

**Admissible evidence:** the PM role's recorded framing; every
Bounded Context's scenario register read in full, never one context's
copy of another's; the solutions architect's decomposition, for where
a scenario lands; the owning shop's steps for a scenario. Not
authoritative: a stakeholder document transcribed into tickets; a
scenario written without the owning shop; this role's own memory of
what the PM meant.

**Interfaces:**
- The PM role: framed intent in; requirements artifacts, backlog
  order, and scope questions out, for the check.

# Process: PO output check

**Purpose:** Check a piece of the PO role's output against the PM
role's framing under criteria the definitions state, so that the PM
role decides from a screen verdict — pass, fail with the criterion
named, or a definition change — and never by reading every artifact.

**Guiding statement:** The check is the criteria applied, not the
checker's reading. A finding the criteria cannot name is a missing
criterion, and the decision that follows is a definition change, not a
verdict on the maker.

**Outcomes:**
- O1. The output is screened against a named criteria set and the
  framing it claims to serve — witnessed by `screen`'s inputs and the
  `screen-review` it returns.
- O2. The PM role decides from the review and round log; the artifact
  reaches the PM role only through the findings' quotes — witnessed by
  `decide`'s inputs, which exclude the artifact.
- O3. Every screen round is recorded and the loop exits on a clean
  verdict, on findings no criterion names, or at the round cap —
  witnessed by `log-round` and `route-screen`.
- O4. A fail names the criterion missed; a definition change names the
  gap, and the gap is filed in the named definition's Document History
  — witnessed by the `check-decision` fields and `record`'s
  `definition` and `gap_entry` outputs.
- O5. A question the framing cannot answer leaves the run as an ask to
  the PM role, with a default, and the run resumes — witnessed by
  `revise`'s `asks` and the `ask` value.

**A. `ancestry: [definition, …]` is wrong for product-decision-record, acceptance-scenarios, backlog-order (confident).**
`definition` is "the generic root for documents that state what good looks like for something else … so a validator that knows only `definition` can check any definition document against the two requirements below." Declaring it means an instance must carry definition's frontmatter — `status (draft | approved | superseded)`, `owner`, `version`, `approved` — and body — an opening before the first heading, "a closing checks section (its heading contains 'check')", Document History last. A decision record, a scenario set, and a backlog order carry none of the checks-section requirement, and each typedef's status set (`draft | checked | returned | pending-definition | …`) contradicts definition's closed set. A validator that knows only `definition` would fail every instance. Required change: drop `definition` from the ancestry of the three (`[product-decision-record]`, `[acceptance-scenarios]`, `[backlog-order]`, after the research-report exemplar's `[research-report]`), or declare a root whose frontmatter and sections these instances actually carry. **B. Derived review checklist entries cite the fitness set, not this typedef's clauses (confident).**

The commitment "a validator can check any instance from it alone" fails when the checklist's clauses live outside. Required change: cite the typedef's own section (`§Required sections 2; §Rules`), keeping the fitness scenario number as a secondary note if wanted.

**C. Opening before the first heading (wobbly, inherited).** definition §Required sections 1: "An opening that states what the document defines before the first section heading." Status sets vs po-output-check (confident on the shared core; wobbly on the extras).** All four carry `checked`, `returned`, `pending-definition` plus `draft` — consistent with the process ("`checked` on pass, `returned` on fail, `pending-definition` on definition change"). 13	# Base writing style
14	
15	These rules apply to everything written for a human reader, regardless of
16	document type. Document types add a format layer on top of this base; they
17	never override it.
18	
19	## Goal
20	
21	The reader gets the point of any paragraph in one read, any section in 30
22	seconds, and the whole document in two minutes. Write for the first read.
23	
24	## Lead with the point
25	
26	At every scale, state the conclusion first and the support after.
27	
28	- A document opens with what it found or decided, not how it got there.
29	- A section opens with its main claim, then evidence.
30	- A paragraph opens with its point, then elaboration.
31	
32	If a document type defines a structure, that structure is just this rule
33	applied to that type. If no structure is defined, use this rule to invent
34	one.
35	
36	## Detail placement
37	
38	Precision serves the point; it never precedes it. Formal specification
39	language, methods, raw data, scoring tables, and citations go after the
40	claim they support — or in an appendix. The body is for understanding.
41	
42	## Sentences
43	
44	- One idea per sentence.
45	- Active voice, with a named actor: "Reviewers delete unlinked checks,"
46	  not "Unlinked checks are subject to deletion."
47	- Prefer the short common word: "use" not "utilize," "end" not
48	  "terminate," "before" not "prior to."
49	
50	## Terminology
51	
52	- Never use a metaphor as a technical term. If a word describes a thing
53	  by what it resembles instead of what it literally does, replace it with
54	  the literal description. Test: could a competent reader from outside
55	  the team work out the meaning from the words alone? If not, rewrite.
56	- Banned words. Never use these, in any form:
57	  - "load-bearing" → say "other work depends on it" or "critical to
58	    operations"
59	  - "surface" (as in context surface, config surface) → say "input,"
60	    "source," or "channel"
61	  - "seam" → say "boundary" or "integration point"
62	  - "scar tissue" → describe the actual problem, e.g. "an unreviewed
63	    workaround that was never removed"
64	- Explain every insider reference — a past incident, an internal system,
65	  a person — in one plain sentence, or cut it. Assume the reader knows
66	  none of our history.
67	
68	## Style examples
69	
70	These examples exist only to show sentence style. The domain (a public
71	library) is deliberately unrelated to our work. Copy the style; never
72	copy the content or vocabulary into real documents.
73	
74	bad:
75	
76	> Unreturned inventory constitutes scar tissue on the circulation loop
77	> and rapidly becomes load-bearing for downstream shelving throughput.
78	
79	good:
80	
81	> Overdue books pile up at the front desk, and staff spend their time
82	> reshelving late returns instead of helping visitors.
83	
84	The bad sentence uses two metaphors as terms and never names an actor.
85	The good sentence says who is affected and what actually happens, in
86	plain words.

107	# Glossary
108	
109	## How the list combines
110	
111	The defined-term list is this glossary combined with every schema element
112	name. Per the `use-defined-terms` principle, a writer choosing between
113	terms uses one of these when one fits.
114	
115	## Terms
116	
117	- **artifact type** — a named, schema-defined document type (e.g.
118	  `decision-brief`); the term the schema registry uses. Not "kind".
119	- **data type** — a named, schema-defined structure that is not a
120	  human-readable document (e.g. `review`); passed between process steps.
121	- **simple type** — a JSON Schema primitive (`string`, `integer`,
122	  `boolean`, `array`, `object`), usable inline without registration.
123	- **typedef** — the single source a type is generated from; templates and
124	  schema fragments are its renderings (owned by shopsystem-knowledge).
125	- **schema** — the machine-checkable shape of a type: fields, types,
126	  enums, required sections.
127	- **process definition** — the source of truth for a process: header
128	  (purpose, outcomes, roles), data section, steps section.
129	- **step** — one unit of a process: an agent step (carries a prompt) or a
130	  runtime step (carries `set`, `run`, or `branches`; no prose).
131	- **rendering** — a generated output of a definition (a skill, a
132	  diagram, a template); never edited by hand, never the source of truth.
133	- **guiding statement** — an optional header element of a process
134	  definition that directs judgment across the whole process; compiled
135	  into every rendering.
136	- **fitness set** — judged (never executed) Given/When/Then scenarios
137	  scoring an artifact type's quality.
138	- **guideline** — prose quality rules for an artifact type, each with a
139	  test, a criterion, and a yes/no decision.
140	- **role** — a named capability contract and set of accountabilities,
141	  assigned by process steps to whoever fills it; sequencing lives in
142	  process definitions, not roles.
143	- **principle** — a standing rule about how we work: name, statement,
144	  rationale, implications (see the principles document's opening
145	  definition).
146	- **seed layer** — the hand-approved definitions the regress terminates
147	  at: the principle set plus one typedef per definition document type.
148	- **owner** — the role that approves changes to a definition; named in
149	  every definition's frontmatter.
150	- **definition chain** — the six linked definitions of good for one
151	  artifact type; required before instances are authored or rewritten.
152	- **keeper** — a corpus record whose action is keep-rewrite; rewritten
153	  forward through its type's approved chain, never used as-is.
154	- **rewrite-forward** — the default for keepers: re-author to the
155	  approved standard; repair-in-place only for records already at the bar.
156	- **rebaseline** — Phase 1 of the re-founding arc: the active tree comes
157	  to hold only chain-conforming records; retired mass moves to the
158	  archive.
159	- **scope** (of a principle set) — the level the set governs and whose
160	  context it loads into: working (every activity), architecture (the
161	  designed system), or experience (the product's interactions).
162	- **transcript** — the runtime log of turns; unscoped, not a governed
163	  artifact, never loaded into context.
164	- **conversation** — a scoped, bounded discussion attached to exactly one
165	  anchor; every conversation belongs to a process.
166	- **anchor** — the governed record a conversation attaches to: a session
167	  record, a review record, or a work item; carries the conversation's
168	  state across transcript boundaries.
169	- **conversation type** — discovery (anchor: a session record), review
170	  (anchor: a review record and its outcomes), or work (anchor: a work
171	  item).
172	- **session record** — the anchor record of a discovery conversation:
173	  outcome, produced and revised lists, open threads, select quotes.
174	- **review** — one bounded conversation in which the authority decides
175	  on presented material. Replaces "sitting".
176	- **review record** — the anchor record of a review: the material
177	  presented and the outcomes applied; each decision traces in the
178	  changed artifacts' Document History, never in a standing ledger.
179	- **park** — the failsafe for work that cannot pass review within its
180	  round cap: set aside with a filed finding.
181	- **round cap** — the declared maximum review rounds before a loop's
182	  failsafe exit fires.
183	- **action** — the approved choice for one record: keep-rewrite, keep,
184	  retire, or terminal, with its target.
185	- **authority-call** — a row marker on a migration-plan row awaiting a
186	  decision from the authority; not an action — the row has no effect and
187	  is out of scope for any run until ruled.
188	- **action table** — the table of records and their actions; approved row
189	  by row or in blocks at a review. Drives any bulk record change.
190	- **close-out** — the mechanical execution of the migration plan's
191	  pre-decided retire and terminal actions: snapshot, delete, archive
192	  move, a loud post-check, and the branch promotion; no review loop.
193	  All stages run consecutively at cut-over.
194	- **snapshot tag** — the annotated git tag (`pre-migration`) on `main`'s
195	  pre-execution commit, preserving the full corpus for terminal-recovery;
196	  after close-out a terminal record exists only there.
197	- **migration plan** — the rebaseline's action table plus the order of
198	  the per-type migration runs. Replaces "rebaseline bill".
199	- **run** — one execution of a process, anchored to a work item; states:
200	  running, held, done, cancelled.
201	- **hold** — a run state: paused with its step and data preserved in its
202	  anchor, by inactivity or by an ask; a held run is resumed or
203	  cancelled, never dropped.
204	- **checkpoint** — updating a conversation's anchor when a transcript
205	  ends mid-conversation; a checkpoint is not a close.
206	- **branched conversation** — a conversation run as a sub-process of
207	  another run; its anchor records the parent (`branched-from`).
208	- **Bounded Context** — a deliberately drawn region of the product with
209	  one internal language, one model, and one set of contracts to other
210	  regions; drawn by design, never discovered after the fact (Evans,
211	  *Domain-Driven Design*).
212	- **shop** — the entity that builds, operates, and evolves part of the
213	  product. Two types: the lead shop (the system-level coordinator; owns
214	  product-level artifacts and no Bounded Context) and the BC-shop (owns
215	  and produces exactly one Bounded Context).
216	- **activity** — a discrete unit of work performed inside a shop,
217	  following a contract or process, with inputs, outcomes, and provenance
218	  recorded. What an actor is stays unconstrained; the activity has the
219	  same shape whoever performs it.
220	- **contract** — a named, versioned statement of what one entity
221	  promises another: the schemas exchanged, the meaning of each
222	  operation, the error behavior, and the relationship kind. Offered as a
223	  product contract (on a Bounded Context) or an operational contract (on
224	  a shop); nothing outside a contract is promised.
225	- **relationship kind** — the named pattern a contract declares for how
226	  two Bounded Contexts relate, drawn from the context-mapping catalogue
227	  (Evans, *Domain-Driven Design*): customer–supplier, conformist,
228	  anti-corruption layer, open host service, published language, shared
229	  kernel, or separate ways.
230	- **vehicle** — the message type a request to a Bounded Context shop
231	  travels in; chosen from the pre-state, never from the request's
232	  wording.
233	- **pre-state** — what a Bounded Context actually is before a change,
234	  read from its contracts and its scenario register, never from its
235	  internals.
236	- **framing** — the PM role's recorded statement of what a request is
237	  about: the originator, the problem taken to be worth solving, and the
238	  outcome it serves; the exclusive decision of `lead-pm`.
239	- **acceptance scenario** — a Gherkin scenario that states, as a
240	  requirement, what counts as done for one behavior; co-produced by the
241	  PO role and the owning Bounded Context shop; held in that shop's
242	  scenario register.
243	- **scenario register** — a Bounded Context shop's own list of the
244	  acceptance scenarios it holds, with their hashes and states; read in
245	  full across every context when a claim spans contexts.
246	- **ask** — a question one activity puts to another role in place of
247	  its output, carrying a default and a checkpoint; the run holds, the
248	  role answers, the step resumes — never a wait in place (data type
249	  `ask`; process-definition typedef §Run lifecycle).
250	- **clarify** — an ask from a Bounded Context shop to the lead shop on
251	  scope, vocabulary, structure, or contract; answered by the role whose
252	  domain the question falls in.
253	- **decomposition** — the solutions architect's record of which Bounded
254	  Context owns which capability, and the relationship kind of each
255	  contract between contexts.
256	- **enabler work** — technical work that makes a feature possible;
257	  recommended by the solutions architect, placed in the backlog by the
258	  PO role.
259	- **interaction type** — one way a person or an agent reaches the
260	  product: command line (CLI), full-screen terminal (TUI), graphical or
261	  web (GUI), API and SDK, conversational, voice, or a generated document
262	  or notification; each honours its own conventions within one
263	  experience. The experience guidelines cover conversational and voice
264	  together as the `assistant` guideline.
265	- **experience guidance corpus** — the product designer role's
266	  principle set and guidelines for the experience: design principles,
267	  vocabulary and voice, core-task parity across interaction types,
268	  interaction patterns per type, and the accessibility target; the
269	  role's exclusive domain.
270	- **originator** — whoever expresses intent at the product's edge: a
271	  person, a shop, or a system outside the product.
272	- **generated interface** — an interface whose form the product composes
273	  at run time from the person's context, within constraints the
274	  experience guidance corpus states; a form, not an interaction type.
275	- **assistant interaction** — an interaction in which the product acts on
276	  an intent the person stated rather than on a command — conversational,
277	  voice, or an assistant acting for the person (a closed set); the locus
278	  of control is the product's, so the experience principles bound it.
279	- **intent** — a desired outcome expressed by an originator at the
280	  product's edge; enters the product through a contract and keeps its
281	  provenance through every translation and delegation.

319	# Lead PO
320	
321	You hold the role that makes the requirements. From the
322	[PM role](lead-pm.md)'s *framing* — its recorded statement of the problem a request is about
323	and the outcome it serves (see the [glossary](../glossary.md)) — you
324	author the artifacts that say what the product is supposed to do:
325	briefs (a bounded statement of a problem and its scope for a Bounded
326	Context shop), product decision records (the record of one
327	product-level decision and its reasons), and acceptance scenarios (see
328	the glossary). The brief and product decision record typedefs are
329	pending on this branch; until they exist, the frozen corpus on `main`
330	is the reference. You order
331	the backlog. Scope and vocabulary questions from any Bounded Context
332	shop resolve against your artifacts. The PM role checks what you make
333	against the framing; you make, you do not check your own work.
334	
335	**Standard of judgment:** you own the commitment, you do not take
336	orders — you decline scope that serves no framed outcome and record
337	the reason. You say what, never how. You author with the shop that
338	owns a behavior, never alone: it supplies the steps and edge cases.
339	
340	**Accountable for:**
341	- Requirements artifacts the rest of the shop can act on — briefs,
342	  product decision records, acceptance scenarios — each traceable to
343	  the framing it serves.
344	- Acceptance scenarios written in Gherkin: each tagged, identified by
345	  a hash of its text so that a changed scenario is a new scenario,
346	  testable against the running system, and co-produced with the
347	  Bounded Context shop that owns the behavior.
348	- The backlog: its content and order within the framing, structured
349	  to mirror the [solutions architect](lead-solutions-architect.md)'s
350	  decomposition.
351	- Scope and vocabulary answers to clarify questions from Bounded
352	  Context shops, grounded in the requirements artifacts.
353	- The requirements picture readable from the artifacts alone, without
354	  asking their author; new domain vocabulary added to the glossary.
355	
356	**Domain (exclusive):** backlog order — this role alone decides which
357	requirement the shops take up next, within the framing.
358	
359	**Decision rights.**
360	- *Decides:* backlog order (exclusive). The content of the artifacts
361	  it submits is this role's authorship and the PM role's check; which
362	  scenario a clarify resolves against is this role's answer, open to
363	  the shop's evidence.
364	- *Recommends:* scope changes to the PM role, with reasons; scenario
365	  splits to the owning Bounded Context shop.
366	- *Places or declines in the backlog, with reasons:* enabler work the
367	  solutions architect recommends — an exercise of the exclusive
368	  domain, not a recommendation.
369	- *Escalates to the PM role:* scope conflicts; a scenario the
370	  solutions architect reports as infeasible or as crossing contexts; a
371	  framing the artifacts cannot be written from.
372	- *Never decides:* whether a problem is worth solving (the PM's); the
373	  pass or fail of its own output (the PM's check); how a behavior is
374	  built (the shops' and the architect's); which context owns a
375	  behavior (the architect's).
376	
377	**Admissible evidence:** the PM role's recorded framing; every
378	Bounded Context's scenario register read in full, never one context's
379	copy of another's; the solutions architect's decomposition, for where
380	a scenario lands; the owning shop's steps for a scenario. Not
381	authoritative: a stakeholder document transcribed into tickets; a
382	scenario written without the owning shop; this role's own memory of
383	what the PM meant.
384	
385	**Interfaces:**
386	- The PM role: framed intent in; requirements artifacts, backlog
387	  order, and scope questions out, for the check.
388	- The solutions architect role: PM-checked scenarios out, for
389	  assignment to the Bounded Context that owns each; enabler recommendations, non-functional constraints, and
390	  decomposition changes in.
391	- Bounded Context shops: scenarios co-produced — this role supplies
392	  scope and wording, the shop supplies steps and edge cases, the
393	  architect supplies context ownership and feasibility; clarify
394	  questions on scope and vocabulary in, answers out.
395	- Asks out, to the PM role: a question the framing cannot answer,
396	  sent with a proposed default.
397	
398	**Knowledge and skills:** requirements authoring; Gherkin as an
399	acceptance language, and the practice it assumes — scenarios written
400	by the business, testing, and development perspectives together
401	("three amigos"); backlog ordering by outcome; the product's domain
402	language; the [working principle set](../principles.md).
403	
404	**Anti-rationalization:**
405	- "The stakeholder's list is the requirement." → A list is input; the
406	  framing decides what serves an outcome.
407	- "I know the domain best, I'll write the scenarios myself." → The
408	  owning shop writes the steps; a scenario without them is not
409	  co-produced.
410	- "It's obviously done." → Done is the PM role's check against the
411	  framing, not this role's opinion of its own output.
412	- "The architect said it can't be built, so drop it." → Infeasible
413	  escalates to the PM role for re-framing; it is not a scope decision
414	  here.
415	- "I'll specify how, it's faster." → The how is the shops'; specifying
416	  it removes their ownership and the architect's check.

454	# Process: PO output check
455	
456	**Purpose:** Check a piece of the PO role's output against the PM
457	role's framing under criteria the definitions state, so that the PM
458	role decides from a screen verdict — pass, fail with the criterion
459	named, or a definition change — and never by reading every artifact.
460	
461	**Guiding statement:** The check is the criteria applied, not the
462	checker's reading. A finding the criteria cannot name is a missing
463	criterion, and the decision that follows is a definition change, not a
464	verdict on the maker.
465	
466	**Outcomes:**
467	- O1. The output is screened against a named criteria set and the
468	  framing it claims to serve — witnessed by `screen`'s inputs and the
469	  `screen-review` it returns.
470	- O2. The PM role decides from the review and round log; the artifact
471	  reaches the PM role only through the findings' quotes — witnessed by
472	  `decide`'s inputs, which exclude the artifact.
473	- O3. Every screen round is recorded and the loop exits on a clean
474	  verdict, on findings no criterion names, or at the round cap —
475	  witnessed by `log-round` and `route-screen`.
476	- O4. A fail names the criterion missed; a definition change names the
477	  gap, and the gap is filed in the named definition's Document History
478	  — witnessed by the `check-decision` fields and `record`'s
479	  `definition` and `gap_entry` outputs.
480	- O5. A question the framing cannot answer leaves the run as an ask to
481	  the PM role, with a default, and the run resumes — witnessed by
482	  `revise`'s `asks` and the `ask` value.
483	
484	**Roles:** maker — [`../roles/lead-po.md`](../roles/lead-po.md)
485	(submits and revises; never decides its own pass). screener —
486	[`../roles/cold-reviewer.md`](../roles/cold-reviewer.md) (fresh
487	context every round; judges against the criteria). the PM role —
488	[`../roles/lead-pm.md`](../roles/lead-pm.md) (accountable for the
489	decision; a human-held role that decides from the verdict; its
490	assisting agent prepares the record and the gap entry).
491	
492	**Carried by:**
493	[`../skills/po-output-check/SKILL.md`](../skills/po-output-check/SKILL.md)
494	— generated from this definition by
495	[`../tools/compile_process.py`](../tools/compile_process.py), never
496	edited by hand.

555	## Steps
556	
557	```yaml
558	start: screen
559	parameters: [artifact, framing, criteria_path]
560	result: decision
561	steps:
562	  - id: screen
563	    name: Screen against the criteria
564	    run-by: {role: cold-reviewer, execution: agent, fresh-context: true}
565	    inputs: [artifact, framing, criteria_path]
566	    outputs: [review]
567	    prompt: |
568	      Read the criteria set at criteria_path, the framing at framing,
569	      and the artifact at artifact — nothing else. Judge the artifact
570	      against every criterion and against the framing: does each part
571	      of it trace to the framing, and does anything in it serve no
572	      framed outcome? Report every finding with the criterion it fails
573	      by name — "framing" for a part that does not trace to the framing
574	      or serves no framed outcome — the quoted text, the change, and
575	      whether you could decide it (confident) or not (wobbly); for a
576	      wobbly finding quote the whole passage, since the PM role decides
577	      from the review alone. A defect no criterion names is a finding
578	      with criterion "uncovered". Verdict "clean"
579	      only if there are no findings; otherwise "findings" with the top
580	      three changes.
581	    next: log-round
582	    annotations:
583	      fabro: {model: high-reasoning, node: separate-context-per-round}
584	
585	  - id: log-round
586	    name: Record the round
587	    run-by: {execution: runtime}
588	    inputs: [review, round_log]
589	    set:
590	      round_log: round_log + [review]
591	    next: route-screen
592	
593	  - id: route-screen
594	    name: Route on the screen
595	    run-by: {execution: runtime}
596	    inputs: [review, round, round_cap]
597	    branches:
598	      - label: "success exit: clean"
599	        when: review.verdict == "clean"
600	        next: decide
601	      - label: "definition exit: every finding is uncovered — nothing the maker can repair"
602	        when: size(review.findings) > 0 && review.findings.all(f, f.criterion == "uncovered")
603	        next: decide
604	      - label: "failsafe exit: round >= round_cap — decide with findings open"
605	        when: round >= round_cap
606	        next: decide
607	      - else: revise
608	
609	  - id: revise
610	    name: Revise the output
611	    run-by: {role: lead-po, execution: agent}
612	    inputs: [artifact, review, framing, ask]
613	    outputs: [artifact]
614	    asks: [lead-pm]
615	    prompt: |
616	      Repair every finding whose criterion is named, "framing"
617	      included; leave findings marked "uncovered" as they are — they
618	      are the PM role's to decide. If a repair needs something the framing does not say —
619	      the originator's intent, whether a thing is in scope, a decision
620	      another role's domain holds — return an ask to lead-pm instead
621	      of guessing: the question, its kind, the default you will apply
622	      if unanswered, and a checkpoint holding the repairs made so far.
623	      On the first pass ask is absent; if it carries an answer or
624	      resolved defaulted, act on it and finish the repairs.
625	    next: advance-round
626	
627	  - id: advance-round
628	    name: Advance the round
629	    run-by: {execution: runtime}
630	    inputs: [round]
631	    set:
632	      round: round + 1
633	    next: screen
634	
635	  - id: decide
636	    name: Decide on the verdict
637	    run-by: {role: lead-pm, execution: human}
638	    inputs: [review, round_log, framing]
639	    outputs: [decision]
640	    prompt: |
641	      From the final review and the round log, decide. "pass": the
642	      screen is clean, or its only findings are uncovered and you judge
643	      none of them needs a criterion — say so in the reasons. "fail": a
644	      named criterion, "framing" included, is still missed at the round
645	      cap — name it.
646	      "definition-change": an uncovered finding should have been a
647	      criterion, or a criterion the output met produced something that
648	      does not serve the framing — name the definition and what it
649	      lacks. Where both a missed named criterion and an open uncovered finding
650	      stand at the cap, "fail" takes precedence and the reasons carry
651	      the uncovered finding. Decide from the quotes in the review.
652	      Record your reasons.
653	    next: record
654	
655	  - id: record
656	    name: Record the decision
657	    run-by: {role: lead-pm, execution: agent}
658	    inputs: [decision, artifact, round_log]
659	    outputs: [artifact, gap_entry, definition]
660	    prompt: |
661	      Write into the artifact's Document History one review entry per
662	      round with its verdict, then a state entry carrying the decision
663	      and its reasons. Set the artifact's status: "checked" on pass,
664	      "returned" on fail with the criterion named, "pending-definition"
665	      on definition-change. On "definition-change", write a review
666	      entry stating the gap into the Document History of the definition
667	      the decision names; return that file's path as definition and the
668	      entry's text as gap_entry. Otherwise return both empty. Return
669	      the artifact.
670	    next: end

710	# Fitness set: brief
711	
712	A brief is the PO role's bounded statement of a problem and its scope
713	for a Bounded Context shop (the typedef is pending on this branch; the
714	frozen corpus on `main` is the reference). These scenarios are the
715	criteria set the [PO output check](../processes/po-output-check.md)
716	screens a brief against, alongside the PM role's framing, which is
717	always the criterion named `framing`. They are evaluated by the
718	`cold-reviewer` role, never executed — no step definitions exist or
719	will exist. The judge's model and prompt version are recorded with each
720	round verdict.
721	The judge reads only the criteria set, the framing, and the artifact;
722	every scenario therefore asks for what the artifact itself carries, and
723	a fact it must carry — a term's definition, a reference, a reason — is
724	what these scenarios make it carry. These scenarios stand in for the
725	pending typedef and are its first draft; the typedef inherits them.

727	## Scenarios
728	
729	Scenario 1: declined scope carries its reason
730	  Given each statement the brief marks out of scope
731	  When it is read
732	  Then it carries the reason it is out of scope

735	  Given the brief's statement of what the shop is asked for

737	  Then it states the problem and the outcome and names no how — no
738	  technology, structure, or interface form the shop would otherwise
739	  choose; naming an interaction type the behavior must hold on is a
740	  what, not a form
741	
742	Scenario 3: scope has an edge

# Base writing style

These rules apply to everything written for a human reader, regardless of
document type. Document types add a format layer on top of this base; they
never override it.

## Goal

The reader gets the point of any paragraph in one read, any section in 30
seconds, and the whole document in two minutes. Write for the first read.

## Lead with the point

At every scale, state the conclusion first and the support after.

- A document opens with what it found or decided, not how it got there.
- A section opens with its main claim, then evidence.
- A paragraph opens with its point, then elaboration.

If a document type defines a structure, that structure is just this rule
applied to that type. If no structure is defined, use this rule to invent
one.

## Detail placement

Precision serves the point; it never precedes it. Formal specification
language, methods, raw data, scoring tables, and citations go after the
claim they support — or in an appendix. The body is for understanding.

## Sentences

- One idea per sentence.
- Active voice, with a named actor: "Reviewers delete unlinked checks,"
  not "Unlinked checks are subject to deletion."
- Prefer the short common word: "use" not "utilize," "end" not
  "terminate," "before" not "prior to."

## Terminology

- Never use a metaphor as a technical term. If a word describes a thing
  by what it resembles instead of what it literally does, replace it with
  the literal description. Test: could a competent reader from outside
  the team work out the meaning from the words alone? If not, rewrite.
- Banned words. Never use these, in any form:
  - "load-bearing" → say "other work depends on it" or "critical to
    operations"
  - "surface" (as in context surface, config surface) → say "input,"
    "source," or "channel"
  - "seam" → say "boundary" or "integration point"
  - "scar tissue" → describe the actual problem, e.g. "an unreviewed
    workaround that was never removed"
- Explain every insider reference — a past incident, an internal system,
  a person — in one plain sentence, or cut it. Assume the reader knows
  none of our history.

## Style examples

These examples exist only to show sentence style. The domain (a public
library) is deliberately unrelated to our work. Copy the style; never
copy the content or vocabulary into real documents.

bad:

> Unreturned inventory constitutes scar tissue on the circulation loop
> and rapidly becomes load-bearing for downstream shelving throughput.

good:

> Overdue books pile up at the front desk, and staff spend their time
> reshelving late returns instead of helping visitors.

The bad sentence uses two metaphors as terms and never names an actor.
The good sentence says who is affected and what actually happens, in
plain words.

# Glossary

## How the list combines

The defined-term list is this glossary combined with every schema element
name. Per the `use-defined-terms` principle, a writer choosing between
terms uses one of these when one fits.

## Terms

- **artifact type** — a named, schema-defined document type (e.g.
  `decision-brief`); the term the schema registry uses. Not "kind".
- **data type** — a named, schema-defined structure that is not a
  human-readable document (e.g. `review`); passed between process steps.
- **simple type** — a JSON Schema primitive (`string`, `integer`,
  `boolean`, `array`, `object`), usable inline without registration.
- **typedef** — the single source a type is generated from; templates and
  schema fragments are its renderings (owned by shopsystem-knowledge).
- **schema** — the machine-checkable shape of a type: fields, types,
  enums, required sections.
- **process definition** — the source of truth for a process: header
  (purpose, outcomes, roles), data section, steps section.
- **step** — one unit of a process: an agent step (carries a prompt) or a
  runtime step (carries `set`, `run`, or `branches`; no prose).
- **rendering** — a generated output of a definition (a skill, a
  diagram, a template); never edited by hand, never the source of truth.
- **guiding statement** — an optional header element of a process
  definition that directs judgment across the whole process; compiled
  into every rendering.
- **fitness set** — judged (never executed) Given/When/Then scenarios
  scoring an artifact type's quality.
- **guideline** — prose quality rules for an artifact type, each with a
  test, a criterion, and a yes/no decision.
- **role** — a named capability contract and set of accountabilities,
  assigned by process steps to whoever fills it; sequencing lives in
  process definitions, not roles.
- **principle** — a standing rule about how we work: name, statement,
  rationale, implications (see the principles document's opening
  definition).
- **seed layer** — the hand-approved definitions the regress terminates
  at: the principle set plus one typedef per definition document type.
- **owner** — the role that approves changes to a definition; named in
  every definition's frontmatter.
- **definition chain** — the six linked definitions of good for one
  artifact type; required before instances are authored or rewritten.
- **keeper** — a corpus record whose action is keep-rewrite; rewritten
  forward through its type's approved chain, never used as-is.
- **rewrite-forward** — the default for keepers: re-author to the
  approved standard; repair-in-place only for records already at the bar.
- **rebaseline** — Phase 1 of the re-founding arc: the active tree comes
  to hold only chain-conforming records; retired mass moves to the
  archive.
- **scope** (of a principle set) — the level the set governs and whose
  context it loads into: working (every activity), architecture (the
  designed system), or experience (the product's interactions).
- **transcript** — the runtime log of turns; unscoped, not a governed
  artifact, never loaded into context.
- **conversation** — a scoped, bounded discussion attached to exactly one
  anchor; every conversation belongs to a process.
- **anchor** — the governed record a conversation attaches to: a session
  record, a review record, or a work item; carries the conversation's
  state across transcript boundaries.
- **conversation type** — discovery (anchor: a session record), review
  (anchor: a review record and its outcomes), or work (anchor: a work
  item).
- **session record** — the anchor record of a discovery conversation:
  outcome, produced and revised lists, open threads, select quotes.
- **review** — one bounded conversation in which the authority decides
  on presented material. Replaces "sitting".
- **review record** — the anchor record of a review: the material
  presented and the outcomes applied; each decision traces in the
  changed artifacts' Document History, never in a standing ledger.
- **park** — the failsafe for work that cannot pass review within its
  round cap: set aside with a filed finding.
- **round cap** — the declared maximum review rounds before a loop's
  failsafe exit fires.
- **action** — the approved choice for one record: keep-rewrite, keep,
  retire, or terminal, with its target.
- **authority-call** — a row marker on a migration-plan row awaiting a
  decision from the authority; not an action — the row has no effect and
  is out of scope for any run until ruled.
- **action table** — the table of records and their actions; approved row
  by row or in blocks at a review. Drives any bulk record change.
- **close-out** — the mechanical execution of the migration plan's
  pre-decided retire and terminal actions: snapshot, delete, archive
  move, a loud post-check, and the branch promotion; no review loop.
  All stages run consecutively at cut-over.
- **snapshot tag** — the annotated git tag (`pre-migration`) on `main`'s
  pre-execution commit, preserving the full corpus for terminal-recovery;
  after close-out a terminal record exists only there.
- **migration plan** — the rebaseline's action table plus the order of
  the per-type migration runs. Replaces "rebaseline bill".
- **run** — one execution of a process, anchored to a work item; states:
  running, held, done, cancelled.
- **hold** — a run state: paused with its step and data preserved in its
  anchor, by inactivity or by an ask; a held run is resumed or
  cancelled, never dropped.
- **checkpoint** — updating a conversation's anchor when a transcript
  ends mid-conversation; a checkpoint is not a close.
- **branched conversation** — a conversation run as a sub-process of
  another run; its anchor records the parent (`branched-from`).
- **Bounded Context** — a deliberately drawn region of the product with
  one internal language, one model, and one set of contracts to other
  regions; drawn by design, never discovered after the fact (Evans,
  *Domain-Driven Design*).
- **shop** — the entity that builds, operates, and evolves part of the
  product. Two types: the lead shop (the system-level coordinator; owns
  product-level artifacts and no Bounded Context) and the BC-shop (owns
  and produces exactly one Bounded Context).
- **activity** — a discrete unit of work performed inside a shop,
  following a contract or process, with inputs, outcomes, and provenance
  recorded. What an actor is stays unconstrained; the activity has the
  same shape whoever performs it.
- **contract** — a named, versioned statement of what one entity
  promises another: the schemas exchanged, the meaning of each
  operation, the error behavior, and the relationship kind. Offered as a
  product contract (on a Bounded Context) or an operational contract (on
  a shop); nothing outside a contract is promised.
- **relationship kind** — the named pattern a contract declares for how
  two Bounded Contexts relate, drawn from the context-mapping catalogue
  (Evans, *Domain-Driven Design*): customer–supplier, conformist,
  anti-corruption layer, open host service, published language, shared
  kernel, or separate ways.
- **vehicle** — the message type a request to a Bounded Context shop
  travels in; chosen from the pre-state, never from the request's
  wording.
- **pre-state** — what a Bounded Context actually is before a change,
  read from its contracts and its scenario register, never from its
  internals.
- **framing** — the PM role's recorded statement of what a request is
  about: the originator, the problem taken to be worth solving, and the
  outcome it serves; the exclusive decision of `lead-pm`.
- **acceptance scenario** — a Gherkin scenario that states, as a
  requirement, what counts as done for one behavior; co-produced by the
  PO role and the owning Bounded Context shop; held in that shop's
  scenario register.
- **scenario register** — a Bounded Context shop's own list of the
  acceptance scenarios it holds, with their hashes and states; read in
  full across every context when a claim spans contexts.
- **ask** — a question one activity puts to another role in place of
  its output, carrying a default and a checkpoint; the run holds, the
  role answers, the step resumes — never a wait in place (data type
  `ask`; process-definition typedef §Run lifecycle).
- **clarify** — an ask from a Bounded Context shop to the lead shop on
  scope, vocabulary, structure, or contract; answered by the role whose
  domain the question falls in.
- **decomposition** — the solutions architect's record of which Bounded
  Context owns which capability, and the relationship kind of each
  contract between contexts.
- **enabler work** — technical work that makes a feature possible;
  recommended by the solutions architect, placed in the backlog by the
  PO role.
- **interaction type** — one way a person or an agent reaches the
  product: command line (CLI), full-screen terminal (TUI), graphical or
  web (GUI), API and SDK, conversational, voice, or a generated document
  or notification; each honours its own conventions within one
  experience. The experience guidelines cover conversational and voice
  together as the `assistant` guideline.
- **experience guidance corpus** — the product designer role's
  principle set and guidelines for the experience: design principles,
  vocabulary and voice, core-task parity across interaction types,
  interaction patterns per type, and the accessibility target; the
  role's exclusive domain.
- **originator** — whoever expresses intent at the product's edge: a
  person, a shop, or a system outside the product.
- **generated interface** — an interface whose form the product composes
  at run time from the person's context, within constraints the
  experience guidance corpus states; a form, not an interaction type.
- **assistant interaction** — an interaction in which the product acts on
  an intent the person stated rather than on a command — conversational,
  voice, or an assistant acting for the person (a closed set); the locus
  of control is the product's, so the experience principles bound it.
- **intent** — a desired outcome expressed by an originator at the
  product's edge; enters the product through a contract and keeps its
  provenance through every translation and delegation.

# Lead PO

You hold the role that makes the requirements. From the
[PM role](lead-pm.md)'s *framing* — its recorded statement of the problem a request is about
and the outcome it serves (see the [glossary](../glossary.md)) — you
author the artifacts that say what the product is supposed to do:
briefs (a bounded statement of a problem and its scope for a Bounded
Context shop), product decision records (the record of one
product-level decision and its reasons), and acceptance scenarios (see
the glossary). The brief and product decision record typedefs are
pending on this branch; until they exist, the frozen corpus on `main`
is the reference. You order
the backlog. Scope and vocabulary questions from any Bounded Context
shop resolve against your artifacts. The PM role checks what you make
against the framing; you make, you do not check your own work.

**Standard of judgment:** you own the commitment, you do not take
orders — you decline scope that serves no framed outcome and record
the reason. You say what, never how. You author with the shop that
owns a behavior, never alone: it supplies the steps and edge cases.

**Accountable for:**
- Requirements artifacts the rest of the shop can act on — briefs,
  product decision records, acceptance scenarios — each traceable to
  the framing it serves.
- Acceptance scenarios written in Gherkin: each tagged, identified by
  a hash of its text so that a changed scenario is a new scenario,
  testable against the running system, and co-produced with the
  Bounded Context shop that owns the behavior.
- The backlog: its content and order within the framing, structured
  to mirror the [solutions architect](lead-solutions-architect.md)'s
  decomposition.
- Scope and vocabulary answers to clarify questions from Bounded
  Context shops, grounded in the requirements artifacts.
- The requirements picture readable from the artifacts alone, without
  asking their author; new domain vocabulary added to the glossary.

**Domain (exclusive):** backlog order — this role alone decides which
requirement the shops take up next, within the framing.

**Decision rights.**
- *Decides:* backlog order (exclusive). The content of the artifacts
  it submits is this role's authorship and the PM role's check; which
  scenario a clarify resolves against is this role's answer, open to
  the shop's evidence.
- *Recommends:* scope changes to the PM role, with reasons; scenario
  splits to the owning Bounded Context shop.
- *Places or declines in the backlog, with reasons:* enabler work the
  solutions architect recommends — an exercise of the exclusive
  domain, not a recommendation.
- *Escalates to the PM role:* scope conflicts; a scenario the
  solutions architect reports as infeasible or as crossing contexts; a
  framing the artifacts cannot be written from.
- *Never decides:* whether a problem is worth solving (the PM's); the
  pass or fail of its own output (the PM's check); how a behavior is
  built (the shops' and the architect's); which context owns a
  behavior (the architect's).

**Admissible evidence:** the PM role's recorded framing; every
Bounded Context's scenario register read in full, never one context's
copy of another's; the solutions architect's decomposition, for where
a scenario lands; the owning shop's steps for a scenario. Not
authoritative: a stakeholder document transcribed into tickets; a
scenario written without the owning shop; this role's own memory of
what the PM meant.

**Interfaces:**
- The PM role: framed intent in; requirements artifacts, backlog
  order, and scope questions out, for the check.
- The solutions architect role: PM-checked scenarios out, for
  assignment to the Bounded Context that owns each; enabler recommendations, non-functional constraints, and
  decomposition changes in.
- Bounded Context shops: scenarios co-produced — this role supplies
  scope and wording, the shop supplies steps and edge cases, the
  architect supplies context ownership and feasibility; clarify
  questions on scope and vocabulary in, answers out.
- Asks out, to the PM role: a question the framing cannot answer,
  sent with a proposed default.

**Knowledge and skills:** requirements authoring; Gherkin as an
acceptance language, and the practice it assumes — scenarios written
by the business, testing, and development perspectives together
("three amigos"); backlog ordering by outcome; the product's domain
language; the [working principle set](../principles.md).

**Anti-rationalization:**
- "The stakeholder's list is the requirement." → A list is input; the
  framing decides what serves an outcome.
- "I know the domain best, I'll write the scenarios myself." → The
  owning shop writes the steps; a scenario without them is not
  co-produced.
- "It's obviously done." → Done is the PM role's check against the
  framing, not this role's opinion of its own output.
- "The architect said it can't be built, so drop it." → Infeasible
  escalates to the PM role for re-framing; it is not a scope decision
  here.
- "I'll specify how, it's faster." → The how is the shops'; specifying
  it removes their ownership and the architect's check.

# Process: PO output check

**Purpose:** Check a piece of the PO role's output against the PM
role's framing under criteria the definitions state, so that the PM
role decides from a screen verdict — pass, fail with the criterion
named, or a definition change — and never by reading every artifact.

**Guiding statement:** The check is the criteria applied, not the
checker's reading. A finding the criteria cannot name is a missing
criterion, and the decision that follows is a definition change, not a
verdict on the maker.

**Outcomes:**
- O1. The output is screened against a named criteria set and the
  framing it claims to serve — witnessed by `screen`'s inputs and the
  `screen-review` it returns.
- O2. The PM role decides from the review and round log; the artifact
  reaches the PM role only through the findings' quotes — witnessed by
  `decide`'s inputs, which exclude the artifact.
- O3. Every screen round is recorded and the loop exits on a clean
  verdict, on findings no criterion names, or at the round cap —
  witnessed by `log-round` and `route-screen`.
- O4. A fail names the criterion missed; a definition change names the
  gap, and the gap is filed in the named definition's Document History
  — witnessed by the `check-decision` fields and `record`'s
  `definition` and `gap_entry` outputs.
- O5. A question the framing cannot answer leaves the run as an ask to
  the PM role, with a default, and the run resumes — witnessed by
  `revise`'s `asks` and the `ask` value.

**Roles:** maker — [`../roles/lead-po.md`](../roles/lead-po.md)
(submits and revises; never decides its own pass). screener —
[`../roles/cold-reviewer.md`](../roles/cold-reviewer.md) (fresh
context every round; judges against the criteria). the PM role —
[`../roles/lead-pm.md`](../roles/lead-pm.md) (accountable for the
decision; a human-held role that decides from the verdict; its
assisting agent prepares the record and the gap entry).

**Carried by:**
[`../skills/po-output-check/SKILL.md`](../skills/po-output-check/SKILL.md)
— generated from this definition by
[`../tools/compile_process.py`](../tools/compile_process.py), never
edited by hand.

## Data

an explicit source. Conditions are CEL expressions over these names. A

artifact's type. The framing is always a criterion, named `framing`;
until a criteria set exists for a type, `criteria_path` names the
framing itself and `framing` is the only named criterion. The artifact

## Steps

```yaml
start: screen
parameters: [artifact, framing, criteria_path]
result: decision
steps:
  - id: screen
    name: Screen against the criteria
    run-by: {role: cold-reviewer, execution: agent, fresh-context: true}
    inputs: [artifact, framing, criteria_path]
    outputs: [review]
    prompt: |
      Read the criteria set at criteria_path, the framing at framing,
      and the artifact at artifact — nothing else. Judge the artifact
      against every criterion and against the framing: does each part
      of it trace to the framing, and does anything in it serve no
      framed outcome? Report every finding with the criterion it fails
      by name — "framing" for a part that does not trace to the framing
      or serves no framed outcome — the quoted text, the change, and
      whether you could decide it (confident) or not (wobbly); for a
      wobbly finding quote the whole passage, since the PM role decides
      from the review alone. A defect no criterion names is a finding
      with criterion "uncovered". Verdict "clean"
      only if there are no findings; otherwise "findings" with the top
      three changes.
    next: log-round
    annotations:
      fabro: {model: high-reasoning, node: separate-context-per-round}

  - id: log-round
    name: Record the round
    run-by: {execution: runtime}
    inputs: [review, round_log]
    set:
      round_log: round_log + [review]
    next: route-screen

  - id: route-screen
    name: Route on the screen
    run-by: {execution: runtime}
    inputs: [review, round, round_cap]
    branches:
      - label: "success exit: clean"
        when: review.verdict == "clean"
        next: decide
      - label: "definition exit: every finding is uncovered — nothing the maker can repair"
        when: size(review.findings) > 0 && review.findings.all(f, f.criterion == "uncovered")
        next: decide
      - label: "failsafe exit: round >= round_cap — decide with findings open"
        when: round >= round_cap
        next: decide
      - else: revise

  - id: revise
    name: Revise the output
    run-by: {role: lead-po, execution: agent}
    inputs: [artifact, review, framing, ask]
    outputs: [artifact]
    asks: [lead-pm]
    prompt: |
      Repair every finding whose criterion is named, "framing"
      included; leave findings marked "uncovered" as they are — they
      are the PM role's to decide. If a repair needs something the framing does not say —
      the originator's intent, whether a thing is in scope, a decision
      another role's domain holds — return an ask to lead-pm instead
      of guessing: the question, its kind, the default you will apply
      if unanswered, and a checkpoint holding the repairs made so far.
      On the first pass ask is absent; if it carries an answer or
      resolved defaulted, act on it and finish the repairs.
    next: advance-round

  - id: advance-round
    name: Advance the round
    run-by: {execution: runtime}
    inputs: [round]
    set:
      round: round + 1
    next: screen

  - id: decide
    name: Decide on the verdict
    run-by: {role: lead-pm, execution: human}
    inputs: [review, round_log, framing]
    outputs: [decision]
    prompt: |
      From the final review and the round log, decide. "pass": the
      screen is clean, or its only findings are uncovered and you judge
      none of them needs a criterion — say so in the reasons. "fail": a
      named criterion, "framing" included, is still missed at the round
      cap — name it.
      "definition-change": an uncovered finding should have been a
      criterion, or a criterion the output met produced something that
      does not serve the framing — name the definition and what it
      lacks. Where both a missed named criterion and an open uncovered finding
      stand at the cap, "fail" takes precedence and the reasons carry
      the uncovered finding. Decide from the quotes in the review.
      Record your reasons.
    next: record

  - id: record
    name: Record the decision
    run-by: {role: lead-pm, execution: agent}
    inputs: [decision, artifact, round_log]
    outputs: [artifact, gap_entry, definition]
    prompt: |
      Write into the artifact's Document History one review entry per
      round with its verdict, then a state entry carrying the decision
      and its reasons. Set the artifact's status: "checked" on pass,
      "returned" on fail with the criterion named, "pending-definition"
      on definition-change. On "definition-change", write a review
      entry stating the gap into the Document History of the definition
      the decision names; return that file's path as definition and the
      entry's text as gap_entry. Otherwise return both empty. Return
      the artifact.
    next: end
```

for a Bounded Context shop (the typedef is pending on this branch; the

every scenario therefore asks for what the artifact itself carries, and
a fact it must carry — a term's definition, a reference, a reason — is
what these scenarios make it carry. These scenarios stand in for the

Scenario 1: declined scope carries its reason
  Given each statement the brief marks out of scope
  When it is read
  Then it carries the reason it is out of scope

Scenario 2: the problem, not the solution
  Given the brief's statement of what the shop is asked for
  When it is parsed for design or implementation choices

  technology, structure, or interface form the shop would otherwise
  choose; naming an interaction type the behavior must hold on is a
  what, not a form

Scenario 3: scope has an edge

  neighbouring
  When each is read against the scope
  Then the brief says whether it is in or out, or names the rule that
  decides

  Given the brief without its author present

  Then every term is defined in the brief or the framing, every
  referenced artifact is linked, and every question the framing or the brief
  itself raises is either answered or listed as open

Scenario 5: the first paragraph states the problem and the outcome

  Then the problem and the outcome are already stated (this set's
  proposal for the typedef, after the decision-brief form)

A product decision record is the PO role's record of one product-level
decision and its reasons (the typedef is pending on this branch; the

# Fitness set: backlog order

A backlog order is the PO role's ordered list of requirements within
the PM role's framing — the PO role's exclusive decision — as submitted for
the PM role's check. These scenarios are the criteria set the
[PO output check](../processes/po-output-check.md) screens an order

every scenario therefore asks for what the artifact itself carries, and
a fact it must carry — a term's definition, a reference, a reason — is
what these scenarios make it carry. These scenarios stand in for the
pending backlog-order typedef — no definition yet treats the order as an
artifact — and are its first draft; the typedef inherits them. Scenario 1 overlaps the
process's `framing` criterion by design: the process passes one
framing and an order spans many. What the
judge cannot catch from the order alone — a recommendation omitted, a
wrong context — is the solutions architect role's to raise through its
interface with the PO role.

## Scenarios

Scenario 1: every item serves a framing
  Given each item in the order
  When its framing reference is read
  Then it names the framing it serves, or is marked declined with a
  reason

Scenario 2: the order states the priority it follows
  Given the order's statement of the roadmap priority it was made
  against
  When the order is compared with that statement
  Then items serving a higher-priority framing precede items serving a
  lower one, or the order states a reason for each exception

Scenario 3: enabler work is placed or declined with reasons
  Given the order's list of enabler recommendations received from the
  solutions architect role
  When the order is read
  Then each recommendation appears in the order with its position
  reasoned, or is declined with a reason

Scenario 4: the order names each item's context
  Given each item
  When it is read
  Then it names the Bounded Context that owns it, and an item crossing
  contexts is marked as such with the escalation to the PM role named

Scenario 5: the next item says whether it is ready
  Given the first item not yet taken up
  When it is read
  Then the order marks it ready and links the brief or scenario set it
  states is checked (passed the PO output check), or marks it not ready
  and names what it waits on

| Scenario Then | Judge-rubric assertion |
|---|---|
